summary: @servicetitan/responsive preinstall drops Bun runtime and executes bundled obfuscated payload
details: package.json declares scripts.preinstall="node setup.mjs". setup.mjs downloads the Bun runtime from github.com/oven-sh/bun release assets, extracts and chmod+x's the binary into a temporary directory, and then invokes it via execFileSync(bunPath, [math_init.js]) against a sibling file shipped in the tarball. math_init.js is a 727 KB single-line bundle marked `// @bun @bun-cjs` with obfuscator.io-style transforms (rotated string array `n7gIxM`, shift routine `WV8StW`, `_0x`-style identifiers). setup.mjs also runs `ldd --version` and reads `/etc/os-release` to detect Alpine/musl and select the matching Bun build so the payload lands on hardened Linux CI images. The package presents itself as a React responsive-UI component library, which has no legitimate need to fetch a second language runtime at install time and use it to execute a heavily obfuscated bundled file. The alternate-runtime invocation is consistent with evading Node-based install-time scanners.

cwes.description: The product contains code that appears to be malicious in nature.
cwes.name: Embedded Malicious Code
